chunks: What doping is and how it is done. The question: What is doping?
Doping means adding a tiny, controlled amount of another element to a semiconductor on purpose. Pure silicon barely conducts.
A few impurity atoms give it many more free carriers, and they set the carrier type: electrons for N-type or holes for P-type.
Doping is how chip makers build every diode, transistor and resistor on a chip.
Think of a nearly empty dance floor with only a handful of dancers. Adding a few more dancers makes it far livelier, and a small number of extra dancers has a big effect.
Dopant atoms are those extra dancers. You do not change the room, only invite a few guests.
The analogy is loose: the dopants also set whether the new carriers are electrons or holes.
The standard doping sequence. The mask decides where doping happens, implantation sets the dose and depth, and the anneal activates the dopants and repairs damage.
Anneals also let dopants diffuse a little, which engineers must budget.
Dopant: the impurity atom added on purpose. Carrier: a free electron or hole that can move and carry current. N-type and P-type: silicon with extra electrons, or extra holes.
Intrinsic: pure silicon with no doping. Ion implantation: firing electrically charged dopant atoms into the silicon slice (wafer), then heating it to repair the damage.
Silicon has about 5 times 10 to the 22 atoms per cubic centimeter (cm³). Add just one phosphorus atom per million silicon atoms.
That is 5 times 10 to the 16 dopant atoms per cm³, each giving one free electron.
Pure silicon has only about 10 to the 10 free carriers per cm³, so doping raises the number about five million times. That is the whole idea.
"Doping is deliberately adding a tiny, controlled amount of impurity atoms to a semiconductor to set its carrier type and concentration.
Pure silicon has only about 10 to the 10 carriers per cm³, so I add phosphorus or arsenic, which each donate an electron for N-type, or boron, which creates a hole for P-type.
A few parts per million is enough to raise conductivity by orders of magnitude.
It's done by ion implantation or diffusion followed by an anneal, and it's how every junction, channel and resistor on a chip is made."
